sections.text:
This procedure details the testing procedures and calibration I1, which 
 recommended to be carried out every year as indicated by Y1 in the title 
 block.

The FTT 7111 has been designed for the protection of power transformers 
 against the risk of over fluxing.

This can cause saturation of the magnetic circuit leading to an increase of 
 the losses. The associated heating should not be maintained for prolonged 
 periods in order to avoid premature ageing of the insulation, which could lead 
 to internal faults to break down.

The flux in the magnetic circuit is proportional to the voltage applied to the 
 transformer, and inversely proportional to its frequency.
 The FTT 7111 relay is supplied from a voltage transformer providing these 
 data.

An image of the flux value is created by means of an integrating circuit 
 whose output voltage, proportional to the ratio v/f, is applied to an 
 adjustable level detecting unit. .

The first draft is initiated by Eng. Mohammed Fahmey Mashaal, tested by Eng. 
 Khalied Diab & Eng. Ehab Abuo Elwafa at 3 September 2008, and accepted by 
 General Manager Eng. Saad Kheder and approved by Eng. Abd Elmoatey Elrakaiby 
 Head Sector of Mahmoudia Power Station.

items:
A work permit must be issued and 
 the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category, 
 (safety helmet, safety shoes, ... etc).

Issue work permit including the 
 team work name.

Safety fence with 
 caution marks surrounding the work area is required.

The unit (generator & 
 transformer) must be out of service.
Secondary injection test set.
Test leads
AVO meter.
Complete tool set.
Air blower.
Contact cleaner (CRC).

Look at Over Flux maintenance file and compare the setting on 
 relay with those shown on the test sheet.

Supply the relay with its nominal auxiliary supply: the green 
 LED will light.
Remove voltage terminals (9,10) from the relay.

Connect the voltage terminals from the injection set to the 
 relay points (9,10).
Increase the injected voltage slowly until pick up.
Record the P.U value in your test sheet.

Decrease the injected voltage until the relay reset (Drop out 
 Value).
Record the D.O value in your test sheet.
Increase the voltage again to (P.U) value.
Stop the test set
Restart the test set (with voltage = P.U value).

The relay will operate, the timer will account and stop when 
 the trip contact close.

Make sure that lock out relays (86GT&86T) operate with over 
 fluxing relay operate.
Record the time value in your test sheet.

Make reset to the over fluxing relay and lock out relays (86GT 
 & 86T).
Put C.B of the unit at local position.
Close C.B of the unit.
Return C.B of the unit to remote position.

Trip C.B of the unit by Over Fluxing Relay by increasing the 
 injection current to the pickup value
Stop the tester.

sections.text: Return Relay and Associated Equipment to Service

items:
Make reset to over fluxing relay, 
 alarm indication and lock out relays (86GT&86T).

Disconnect the test 
 leads from the relay.

Reconnect voltage 
 terminals (9-10) to the relay.

Make sure PT 
 secondary circuits are in normal condition.
